    The PA will be provided a safe and secure full-size vehicle for this transport. The options available to the PA in obtaining the full-size vehicle include utilizing their assigned vehicle, a caged car or a pool car. PAs will not be held liable for safety equipment stored in the passenger compartment of the flexible fuel vehicle that does not provide adequate storage space. Safety equipment other than a firearm may be stored in a State vehicle’s trunk, DAPO-issued secured locked storage compartment or secured inside the Parole Agent’s residence overnight.
  5. Parolees with Infectious Diseases
    1. The State will make available to all PAs Departmentally-approved disposable protective clothing kit to be used as needed. The disposable protective clothing kit will include a fluid-resistant coverall, eye-shield/goggle, latex gloves, disposable paper mask, TB masks and any other protective equipment deemed appropriate by the Department.
    2. The Department will continue to provide PAs updated information regarding Departmental policy and procedures and other information concerning the handling of infectious incarcerated persons and parolees.
    3. The Department will provide to each parole unit, and update as needed, a listing of the designated CDCR Chief Medical Executives for each institution.
    4. The Department has developed protocols for handling biohazardous material and adequately train each PA in the protocol. The State shall provide each PA with a bloodborne pathogen cleanup kit that is carried in the PA’s ready bag and transported from vehicle to vehicle. Additionally, each parole unit/complex and day reporting center shall have biohazardous material disposal “containers”.
  6. The State shall provide a gun locker and/or secured storage locker at the PA’s worksite.
  7. The Department agrees to provide access to a radio and/or cellular telephone to each PA.

19.02 CDCR PA Training

  1. The Department shall attempt to provide reasonable advance notice of scheduled mandatory training.
  2. All Agents shall be armed and carry either the Departmentally-issued semi-automatic pistol, or a personal, Departmentally-approved semi-automatic pistol, and ammunition.
  3. An Agent wishing to carry a personal, Departmentally-approved semi-automatic pistol, may do so only after successfully completing an approved Departmental instruction course. The Department will authorize at the Parole Agent’s expense, the ability to purchase and install Departmentally-approved options, e.g., night sights, adjustable sights, aftermarket stocks (grips) and factory authorized or approved modifications for accuracy and/or ease of use. The Agent shall adhere to the rules, policies and directives of the Department in the use, wearing and maintenance of the weapon. Participation in this program is voluntary. Prior to participation, the PA must sign the agreed upon Participation Agreement.
  4. This weapon may only be carried in properly designated holster(s) which have been approved by the Department.
  5. The Agent shall attend the prescribed initial optional weapons training program on State time.
    1. The Agent shall be allowed to drive their State vehicle to and from any range training and be allowed to transport their personally-owned, Departmentally-approved weapon.
    2. The Department shall provide the Agent Departmentally-approved ammunition necessary to initially qualify on the optional weapon and for quarterly re-qualifications.
    3. The Agent shall carry only Departmentally-issued ammunition for on-duty use of the weapon.
  6. PAs shall be allowed to use CDCR ranges and/or permit/licensed private or public ranges for off-duty practice with either the State-issued weapon, or the Agent’s personal, Departmentally-approved weapon. Ammunition and/or permit/licensed private range fees will be incurred by the PA.
  7. Should the employee fail to qualify on the first attempt, or qualify but still have deficiencies that need to be addressed, the employee shall be provided an opportunity to re-qualify/remediate as soon as possible, which, depending upon availability of slots, and Range Master’s approval, could potentially be the same day or at the next scheduled range or shooter’s clinic. PAs may attend shooter’s clinics/Firearms Skills Training (FST) on a voluntary basis. Agents who have been mandated by the Range Master for remediation shall be given a reason for that mandated remediation. Failure to qualify shall not be the sole determining factor in mandating remedial training (shooter’s clinic).

    Any PA who fails to achieve a qualifying score within the quarter will surrender the State-issued firearm to the Regional Parole Administrator or designee. If a PA, who as a condition of employment is issued a firearm, does not qualify within thirty (30) calendar days of the end of the calendar quarter in which they have failed, the PA shall be placed on leave without pay for no longer than sixty (60) calendar days until said PA qualifies. Failure to qualify during this period of time will result in the PA being separated from State service pursuant to Government Code Section 19585, or other applicable Government Code section(s). However, the employee shall receive at least seven (7) calendar days’ written notice of separation from State service, if personally served, and at least ten (10) calendar days’ written notice, if served by mail.
  8. Parole Agents shall participate in the Parole Agent Safety and Tactical Training (PAST) no more than once per quarter and no less than once annually as determined by the DAPO Director. The DAPO Director may waive up to three (3) of the non-mandated PAST trainings annually and may replace that training with other Departmentally-approved training (e.g., SIMS, MILO, Entry, New Legislation, etc.) and shall inform the CDCR Chief of Labor of the waiver who in turn will inform the CCPOA Chief of Labor.
  9. CDCR and CCPOA agree that the State shall establish and maintain all training records pertaining to the Parole Agent classification. The State shall provide a written record of training to the Parole Agent within forty-five (45) days of the written request.
  10. In the event of mandatory Departmental training for Agents, the Department will determine the need for reduction in specifications/overtime and notify the Agent in writing that the reduction in specifications/overtime is available if requested.

    Overtime requests related to such training hours will be submitted to the requesting Agent’s supervisor on a STD 682. Denials of overtime or modifications to requested hours will be documented, with the reason for denial, on the STD 682 by the requesting Agent’s supervisor.

    To the greatest extent possible, yearly training mandates (including the number of hours required to complete the training) set forth by DAPO shall be provided to CCPOA Headquarters with a copy of the corresponding training materials (which are subject to change) annually on a calendar basis prior to the implementation of yearly training.

    All DAPO-required training shall be conducted during on-duty hours.

    Any time DAPO issues or rescinds a statewide policy, directive, or informational memoranda, DAPO agrees to notify all affected DAPO BU 6 staff and the CDCR Chief of Labor who will notify the Parole Chapter President and the CCPOA Chief of Labor via email or memorandum of the policy issuance or rescission.

19.03 CDCR PA Workweek

  1. Parole Agents (excluding Community Compliance Unit [CCU])

    The normal work schedule for CDCR PAs shall be a four- (4-) or five- (5-) day workweek, as dictated by the workload, and approved by the supervisor in accordance with Subsection D. below. PAs may schedule, with supervisory approval, other than an eight- (8-) or ten- (10-) hour day. When requesting a four- (4-) or five- (5-) day workweek one (1) shift shall include an additional hour to make up for the forty-one (41) hour mandate. The workweek shall start on Monday and end on Sunday.

    PAs may elect the daily start and stop times, with the exception of the Officers of the Day (OD) duty. OD schedules shall be equitable and follow a consistent pattern (e.g., alphabetical order) taking into consideration vacation and leave schedules.

    Work hours, subject to supervisor approval, will be scheduled between 0600 and 2200, except as emergency and operational needs dictate. The basis for denials due to emergency/operational needs shall be articulated in writing by the supervisor. The workday may include, at an employee’s discretion, no meal break, or an optional one (1) hour, or one-half (½) hour meal break which shall occur approximately in the middle of the workday.

    Certain core hours of 0700 to 1800 may be established for PAs in administrative assignments. A work schedule may be denied to fulfill the need to cover these core hours. The rejection of one or more schedules because of this need to cover core hours shall not be deemed a blanket denial.

    If there are no volunteers, the necessary core hour coverage in the administrative assignments shall be determined by inverse seniority.
  2. No work will be routinely scheduled between the hours of 2200 and 0600. Each workday will be a minimum of at least four (4) work hours and a maximum not to exceed twelve (12) work hours, except as emergency and operational needs dictate.
  3. Work schedules shall include a minimum of four (4) evenings/early mornings per month with evening meaning until at least 1900 hours and early morning meaning starting at 0600 unless waived by the supervisor at the request of the PA. At least two (2) of the four (4) shifts must be evenings. Such evenings/mornings shall be in the field, except if previously waived by the supervisor. This shall not prohibit PAs from scheduling additional voluntary evenings/early mornings.
  4. Each PA shall submit a proposed work schedule to the supervisor for each month at least seven (7) calendar days, but no more than fourteen (14) calendar days, prior to the beginning of the scheduled month for supervisory approval. The State shall develop and standardize a work schedule form to be utilized statewide. The schedule will represent all work hours, which shall include all workdays, weekend work, evening work, days off, OD duties and other special assigned responsibilities.

    The supervisor shall approve the work schedule at least three (3) days prior to the scheduled month, unless it can be documented that the scheduled work hours as submitted would be detrimental to the needs of the office or would hinder the PA in the performance of their duties and responsibilities. This documentation shall be provided if requested by the employee in an email or other electronic communication. If the PA does not submit a monthly work schedule, the supervisor will assign the work schedule.

    During the scheduled month, the supervisor may adjust the work hours based on operational needs, with written justification to the PA. This adjustment shall not be utilized to avoid the assignment of overtime. PA requested changes in the work schedules, excluding emergencies, will require prior supervisory approval. PAs will advise the supervisor of emergency changes no later than the next workday.
  5. Recognizing the need for representatives from local enforcement agencies to contact PAs during non-scheduled work hours and days about parolee/incarcerated persons assigned to their supervision, PAs shall have their home telephone or contact number on file with all local law enforcement agencies in the geographical area covered by the PA’s assigned unit. A State contracted answering service will comply with the above needs.
  6. Should a PA need to respond in person to such calls, the PA shall receive a minimum of four (4) hours call-back and shall be compensated in accordance with other provisions of this MOU (e.g., Section 11.12).
  7. Travel Time
    1. Office days: When a PA has an “Officer of the Day” duty or when they have to go to the office at the beginning of their shift, the PA shall be paid beginning at the time of arrival at the office, unless that PA began their workday in the field.
    2. Field days: When the PA leaves their home and travels to a field contact, hours of work shall start on the arrival of the PA at the field contact location. If it takes longer to travel from the PA’s home to the field contact location than the amount of time it takes the PA to travel from their home to the office, then the PA’s work time shall start at the interval of time the PA usually uses to get to work. 
    3. Emergencies or call-back: If the PA is requested to respond to an emergency or suffers any other work before arriving at the office, field contact location or traveling for the period of time it usually takes to get to the office, the PA’s workday shall start at the moment they suffer work.
    4. The Department shall enforce the sixty-five (65) mile (as the crow flies) resident limit for all PAs with a home storage permit subject to State Vehicle Home Storage Permit rules.

      PAs will not be administratively transferred more than fifty (50) miles from their residence.
  8. PAs may work as two (2) person team(s) with prior supervisory approval.

19.04 CDCR PA Standby

  1. Standby is defined as an assignment whereby a PA must remain physically and geographically able to respond when contacted by telephone or electronic device. The assignment shall be in addition to the Agent’s normal work schedule.

    The State will determine when and where standby assignments and back-up PAs’ assignments will be made. The PA will be notified in writing at least three (3) working days prior to the start of the standby assignment. Operational needs may prevent the State from notifying the PA of the standby assignment three (3) working days prior to the assignment, however, the PA shall be notified in writing prior to the start of the standby assignment.
  2. Any time a PA is on standby, they shall receive two (2) hours of compensation per day (straight time pay).

19.05 CDCR PA Caseload Audits and Monthly Roster Reconciliations

  1. PA II Supervisors, PA IIIs, Parole Administrators or their equivalent will complete all audits and monthly roster reconciliations.

    An audit identifies deficiencies for a specified time period.

    The person performing the audit or monthly roster reconciliation shall, within ten (10) workdays of the completion of the audit or monthly roster reconciliation, provide to that PA a written summary of the audit or monthly roster reconciliation.

    A monthly roster reconciliation covers the current month’s workload or a supervisory review of the previous month. Management retains the right to review rosters and a monthly roster reconciliation does not include every time management reviews rosters or accesses data contained in them.

    Audits or roster reconciliations for the previous month shall identify deficiencies, requirements that are/were waived as a result of excessive caseload, all Departmentally-recognized absences and those areas that the PA is performing to expectations or higher.
  2. Grievances under this Section may be grieved according to Article VI of this MOU but shall only be arbitrable under the mini-arb process described in Section 6.13.
  3. This provision shall only apply to DAPO PAs.
  4. If possible, audits of State vehicles will be performed on the Parole Agent’s OD or Unit meeting day.
  5. In order to address discrepancies in a timely fashion, when appropriate and reasonable, Agents will be allowed to be present during case audits.

19.06 Parole Agent and Parole Services Associate Requested Transfers (PART)

  1. The Division of Adult Parole Operations (DAPO) has varying business needs to fill vacant positions by using existing eligible lists, involuntary transfers, reassignments, Academy hires, Executive Orders, program closures, or other selection methods based on, for example, balancing the work force, or pre-announced specialized skills, abilities or aptitudes. The parties agree that DAPO will post new PA I, PA II Specialist, (PA, hereafter) and Parole Services Associate (PSA) seniority lists semi-annually on the intranet. Further, DAPO will provide updated seniority lists as well as a PART vacancy list thirty (30) calendar days prior to the initiation of the PART process. DAPO shall not exclude geographic locations from participating in the PART process.

    The parties acknowledge that PAs/PSAs may want to transfer to another Region/Complex/Unit within DAPO. Therefore, the following seniority-based procedure, which is consistent with Section 12.01 of the MOU, is established to facilitate a PA’s/PSA’s request to transfer within the same classification but different location consistent with this section.
  2. PAs and PSAs cannot utilize this process to either transfer between Units within the same Complex or transfer out of a Complex that has a vacancy rate of more than fifteen percent (15%). For purposes of determining the vacancy rate, Complexes shall not be divided by Districts (when there are multiple Districts in one Complex) and adjacent buildings are included in the Complex. Court Agent, Notice Agent, and Administrative Assignments are ineligible for this PART process.

    The following shall count as a filled position when calculating the Complex vacancy rate:
    1. A position number in which a PA/PSA has been appointed and is currently working;
    2. Out-of-Class (OOC) or Training and Development assignments;
    3. Military leave;
    4. Medical or personal leave (e.g., Workers’ Compensation, FMLA/CFRA, disability accommodation, extended sick/annual leave, non-medical/non-industrial leave, etc.); and
    5. Temporary Voluntary or Involuntary Reassignments.
  3. PAs in a non-specialized caseload can only transfer to a non-specialized caseload or GPS Sex Offender Agent caseload. PAs in a specialized caseload can transfer to the same specialized caseload or a non-specialized caseload. PA II Specialists may transfer between Electronic Monitoring Unit (EMU), Reentry Unit, Sex Offender Unit (SOU), Interstate Compact Unit (ICU), and Community-Based Programs (i.e., Male Community Reentry Program [MCRP] and Female Community Reentry Program [FCRP]) assignments within DAPO. PSAs may transfer between Community Transition Program (CTP), Division Intelligence Unit (DIU), Reentry Immigration and Naturalization Services (INS) Unit, SOU, EMU, and Field PSA assignments within DAPO.
  4. PAs and PSAs desiring to transfer must submit to the applicable Regional Headquarters a Standard Application Form 678 and CDCR Form 923, which shall identify the desired District(s)/Complex(es)/Unit(s) and the numerical order of preference. The employee’s written requests shall be processed at the Regional Headquarters within thirty (30) calendar days of submission and placed in seniority order with the others who have requested transfer to the same District(s)/Complex(es)/Unit(s). The Hiring Authority or designee shall provide the PA(s) and/or PSA(s) submitting a request for transfer with an acknowledgment of receipt of the transfer request within thirty (30) calendar days from the initial transfer request being placed.
  5. PA/PSA requests shall be kept on file at the applicable Regional Headquarters through June 30 of each fiscal year or removed earlier at the request of a PA/PSA. All requests shall be (re)submitted on or after the following July 1. At the request of CCPOA, the location of and access to a PA’s/PSA’s transfer file will be provided to the CCPOA Representative. DAPO shall utilize and maintain a real-time SharePoint or similar technology to track active transfer requests. The SharePoint or similar technology will be accessible to the Parole Chapter President or designee and each of the designated Parole Region PART coordinators.
  6. DAPO agrees to fill vacancies in PA/PSA classifications by either lateral transfers, list appointments, reinstatements, closures, training and development or permanent full-time appointments from the Academy. In the interest of continuously facilitating lateral transfers, the Regional/Unit Managers will determine the number of vacant positions to be filled in a given District/Complex/Unit and will fill at least every other vacancy via lateral transfer until all requests for that District/Complex/Unit have been exhausted. In the event of a closure or merger, involuntary reassignments will be considered a DAPO selection resulting in the same number of lateral transfers being credited to CCPOA. The parties acknowledge and agree that decreases in funding/population may delay a PART move or eliminate previously available vacancies. A decrease in position authority may delay a corresponding PART move until a vacancy becomes available, at which time the parties shall be made whole. PART transfers for DAPO HQ and Northern and Southern Parole HQs shall be based upon three (3) separate lists: Parole Agent I, Parole Agent II Specialist, and PSA. The PA I list shall have no impact on the PA II Specialist or PSA PART transfers. PA Is, PA II Specialists and PSAs shall only compete with others in the same classification. The qualifying senior BU 6 employee on each of these lists shall be granted a PART and the process will proceed with the next qualifying most senior BU 6 member in that classification, until such time as the list is exhausted or no more vacant positions exist. All qualifying vacancies will be filled by the PART process until such time as the PART transfer list is exhausted. The effective date of transfer shall be agreed upon by the sending and receiving Hiring Authority(s), within thirty (30) calendar days following approval.

    With respect to the unique situation of Academy hires (including those currently attending the Academy or hired to be filled from a future Academy), the positions being held for successful graduates are not considered vacant. They are considered a DAPO selection for PART purposes when the graduate reports to the assignment at the DAPO work location, which results in the next vacancy being filled through PART/lateral transfer.
  7. The parties agree to meet not less than once per quarter to reconcile updates/changes to any position authority, to review and reconcile all PART requests/moves from the prior quarter to ensure the one (1) for one (1) PART process referenced in Subsection F. is maintained, and to discuss PART-related issues unless there are no transfer requests on file for the specified District/Complex/Unit.

    As part of the ongoing PART process, DAPO will provide the following information at least quarterly to the CCPOA Parole Chapter President or designee via email or share drive/SharePoint (and at least thirty [30] days prior to any quarterly scheduled PART Committee meeting): the DAPO Position Authority Report (PAR), the updated tracking system log, seniority rosters for the DAPO positions consistent with this Section and updated vacancy reports (PAR includes by Unit and the tracking log includes by each Complex), and the list of outstanding position moves after reviewing the previous quarter’s PART moves, reconciliation of vacant positions, lateral transfer requests, and lateral transfers. CCPOA will identify and provide any discrepancies back to the State within fifteen (15) calendar days prior to the quarterly PART Committee meeting.

    Any disputes regarding the development/maintenance of the tracking system (e.g., the documents to be used or provided, budget authority, vacancies, transfer reconciliation, equitable filling of statewide vacancies) that the PART Committee is unable to resolve will be elevated to the CDCR Undersecretary of Operations and the CCPOA Executive Vice President for final resolution through the CDCR and CCPOA Chiefs of Labor.

    Positions filled with a PA/PSA, including those on leave or serving in an OOC assignment, will be reflected on the monthly Position Authority Report (PAR).

    The “Vacant” column on the PAR will reflect unencumbered positions.

    PART applications must be submitted by 11:59:59 pm on the eighth (8th) calendar day of the month to be effective the same month.

    PART Tracking Logs will be uploaded into the PART Microsoft Teams share drive (or any successor database/share drive) by 12:30 pm on the 20th of each month. Should the 20th fall on a weekend or holiday, then the Tracking Log shall be uploaded by 5pm on the day before the weekend or holiday.

    To ensure position movement tracking accuracy, “hardship” transfers will be identified on the “Moves” tab of the Tracking Log, although they are not included/considered in the PART process.
  8. When PART is the means being used to fill a vacant position, the most senior employee with a request to transfer on file at that location shall be transferred unless there is clear evidence that such a transfer would be adverse to the best interest of the Department, for example, the employee (1) is currently under investigation for misbehavior which could lead to adverse action, (2) the employee does not have an unexpired adverse action in their Official Personnel File or (3) has had an overall substandard performance evaluation in the preceding twelve (12) months. In addition, in order to be eligible for transfer under this section, the employee must have been employed by DAPO as a PA or PSA for more than twenty-four (24) months immediately prior to the PART transfer request and must have completed the DAPO apprenticeship program if applicable. Those employees who accept a PART transfer under the provisions of this Section shall not be eligible to utilize the provisions of this section for a period of two (2) years from the effective date of such a transfer unless the employee has demonstrated a hardship that did not exist at the time of the initial transfer. In the event that the DAPO moves a PA/PSA due to involuntary transfer, that PA/PSA shall be eligible to participate in the PART process again even though they did not serve the full two (2)-year requirement, subject to seniority and all other PART requirements.
  9. Management Selections

    A management selection (or pick) is available throughout a rolling twelve- (12-) month period, which starts the month the selection is received (e.g., a management selection received September 2025 expires September 2026).

    DAPO will document the reason a management selection is being exercised or held on the PART tracking log in the “Moves” tab (e.g., academy hire, administrative placement, confidential reason such as a reasonable accommodation, population fluctuation, etc.). When population fluctuation is listed as the reason, DAPO will discuss and provide supporting documentation at the quarterly PART Committee meeting.

    A management selection to a vacant position will be held only until the original twelve- (12-) month period expires (e.g., For a management selection received in September 2025 and exercised in March 2026, the vacant position being held by the management selection can be held only until the management selection expires in September 2026). After twelve (12) months, if a position remains vacant, it can be filled via PART.

    At units with multiple vacancies, where there are no pending PART requests, DAPO can exercise multiple management selections at one time.
  10. This procedure may be superseded in favor of an employee receiving a transfer based on a bona fide hardship. If the transfer is contested, the Hiring Authority or designee shall explain the basis for the waiving of this section to CCPOA’s Representative.
  11. Travel Time Allowance: Upon request, the State may authorize an employee to take a reasonable amount of vacation, PLP, CTO, furlough or holiday time off between transfers from one (1) location to another where the transfer requires the employee to move their residence at their own expense. Such requests will not be unreasonably denied by the receiving District/Complex/Unit.
  12. During the term of this MOU, DAPO will continue to utilize a one (1) for one (1) job exchange (i.e., two [2] people of the same classification want to exchange Field Unit to Field Unit locations).
  13. After six (6) months from the date of final activation of the Community Reentry Unit (CRU), a portion of the main table teams of DAPO and CCPOA agree to meet and confer on a mutually agreeable, single date (up to eight [8] hours) to jointly determine the sole issue of the date upon which CRU will be added to the list of units listed in Subsection C. above to which PA II Specialists may transfer.

19.07 CDCR PA’s Use of State Vehicles

  1. State vehicles may be made available for those parole staff at their work locations for use during the scheduled workday. A parole staff person, with prior supervisory approval, may be permitted temporary overnight home storage of a State vehicle based on workload or operational needs.
  2. PAs, with prior supervisory approval, may be authorized to use their private vehicle and be reimbursed for mileage.
  3. Specially funded programs which provide State vehicles for PA Is and IIs are excluded from this provision.
  4. State vehicles assigned to PAs shall have adequate trunk space to accommodate safety equipment. Depending on the availability of a vehicle with adequate trunk space, PAs currently assigned flexible fuel vehicles shall have the option of exchanging them.
  5. The parties agree there shall be no marked vehicles (i.e., “CA Exempt” plates) for BU 6 Parole Agents during the term of this MOU. Normally, PAs will not be assigned caged vehicles, except when requested by a PA or in temporary circumstances where a caged vehicle better meets operational/safety needs (e.g., sweeps, specialized task force, etc.).

19.08 Authorizing Overtime and/or Modifying Case Supervision Specifications

  1. The Assistant Deputy Director (ADD) or designee shall delegate the authority to approve overtime to the Unit Supervisor (US), unless compelling circumstances require the authority to be elevated. The authority shall be elevated to a classification no higher than a Parole Administrator where appropriate, in order to manage excessive use of overtime. 
  2. Caseload-Related Management Considerations

    Workload adjustments and overtime approval shall be evaluated on a weekly basis giving due consideration to workload outside of case count (there shall be no mandate to be at the maximum caseload to receive overtime/waiver considerations).

    The US shall implement the following process in order to reduce and/or eliminate the need for overtime during the normal workweek. The US shall:
    1. Ensure adherence to the work schedule consistent with current MOU as it relates to the administration of workload.
    2. Ensure PAs are not scheduled to work more than forty-one (41) total hours in the seven (7) day 7k work period when approving each month’s work schedule.
    3. Ensure the PA does not schedule a regular day off (RDO) on a day when the PA has any other work commitments requiring their attendance, such as scheduled Officer of the Day duties.
    4. Review caseload rosters for scheduled releases and mandatory pickups and/or case contacts pursuant to Penal Code Section 3060.7.
    5. Upon request of a PA, the US will review the PA’s caseload roster with the PA.
    6. The State shall fill vacant positions and/or new positions in a timely manner.
  3. RDOs

    Consistent with long-standing practice, RDOs shall be consecutive and follow a consistent pattern during each week, unless specifically requested by the PA.
  4. Ratio-Driven Caseload Management Considerations
    1. California Parole Supervision and Reintegration Model (CPSRM) Caseloads

      The approved workload for non-specialized caseloads shall be 53:1. This includes the following levels of supervision: Transition Phase (TP), Categories A, B, C, D, E, P, EX, EO, MX, OH, PD, DP, IS, IM, MD and Transfer Investigation Request (TIR) active cases, PALs at the High Control and Specialized level are included in the total number of cases. The exceptions are listed below:

      The approved Enhanced Outpatient Program (EOP) participant caseload ratio shall be 40:1.
    2. Specialized Active Global Positioning System (GPS) Caseload

      The approved GPS gang and GPS sex offender caseload ratio shall be 25:1. The ratios will include in-custody cases, which will be no more than five (5) for GPS gang caseloads. EOPs assigned to the GPS unit shall be distributed equitably amongst all GPS Agents in unit.
    3. Currently, GPS sex offender agents participate in DAPO’s Pre-Release Video Conference (PRVC) program for sex offender pre-parole cases, which may expand to PAs and pre-parole cases generally during the term of this MOU subject to meet and confer requirements.
  5. Caseload Distribution

    DAPO will ensure that twenty-five percent (25%) of the average PA workload in the unit, regardless of supervision category, will not be assigned to PA Is. This caseload percentage should be proportionate to the equitable breakdown of cases by category being supervised within the Parole Unit and reflected on the workload summary. Under no circumstances shall the number of category D cases of this caseload percentage be disproportionate to such assignments for the other PAs in the Unit. The District Administrator will regularly review these case counts to ensure that cases are distributed in an equitable manner.
  6. Workload Ratio Special Considerations

    The US shall address workload in excess of the approved workload ratio within a Parole Unit. When a Unit has an excessive workload, excess cases shall be assigned equitably to all PAs in the unit. The State shall endeavor to distribute pre-parole and TIR cases equitably, taking into account geography and current workloads.

    The differential in caseloads between PAs shall not exceed 10% with due consideration to equitable distribution.

    Exceptions to ratios within a unit can be considered for the PA(s) assigned to caseloads meeting the following criteria or under the following circumstances:

    1. Rural caseloads that require excessive vehicle travel to complete supervision specifications.
    2. Urban caseloads in an area with heavy traffic congestion.
    3. Caseloads in areas where inclement weather conditions result in modified driving conditions, such as chain requirements.
    4. PAs that are current participants in the apprenticeship program.
    5. PAs required participating in the Field Training Program.
    6. Other reasonable circumstances to include time spent away on OB/RTB.
    Only PA Is and PA IIs who have successfully completed the PA Academy, or have been placed into (1) an out-of-class assignment or (2) a training and development assignment, shall be reflected on the Unit Workload Summary. If a PA separates, is on Enhanced Industrial Disability Leave or on any other long-term absence (defined as greater than thirty [30] days), they shall be immediately removed from the Unit Workload Summary. All cases assigned to such a PA shall be reassigned to an active PA I or PA II within the Parole Unit. Under no circumstances shall an active, revoked, suspended or pre-parole case be assigned to a PA III, Parole Services Associate or any support staff, excluding the Regional Re-entry Unit and the Intelligence Unit. Pending assignment, such cases, however, may be placed briefly (for a few hours) with the US, provided that such cases shall be reassigned to PA Is or PA IIs and the US shall be removed from the workload roster by the close of business each day.
  7. CPSRM Unit Workload Summary

    Beginning on the first workday of each month, the US or designee shall utilize the Unit Workload Summary Report to review and adjust the assigned workload for each case carrying agent within the assigned Parole Unit on a weekly basis. Upon review, the US or supervisory peace officer designee shall attempt to balance the unit workload and maintain an equitable mix of categories on each caseload. No PA shall have more than forty (40) parolees in either the “TP” or Category “A” to include EOP or Mentally Disordered Offender (MDO) combined. The remaining cases shall consist of cases that include, but are not limited to: from Categories “B,” “C,” and/or “D,” “E,” “P,” “EX,” “IS,” “IM,” “EO,” “MX,” “OH,” “PD,” “DP,” and “MD.”

    PALs at the High Control and Specialized level are included in the total number of cases. There shall be no more than four (4) EOP cases assigned to a 53:1 caseload, except as described below. These cases shall be designated as “EX” and shall be supervised pursuant to the EOP cases specifications, except in the following circumstances:
    1. There is a sufficient number of EOP, including MDO, cases assigned to a Parole Unit or Complex to create a 40:1 specialized EOP caseload. EOP Specialized caseloads may be established if there are a minimum of thirty-two (32) cases. The approved 40:1 caseload ratio may be exceeded under the following circumstances: (1) a parolee previously supervised who is now in custody or PAL or (2) an excessive Unit workload situation as described above.
    2. If there are insufficient numbers of EOP cases to form an EOP Specialized caseload, the EOP shall be placed on a 53:1 caseload. No more than four (4) EOP, including MDO, cases shall be placed on any non-specialized caseload except in situations where there are not enough case carrying agents (less than eight [8] PAs in a unit) to allow for four (4) EOPs per agent and less than thirty-two (32) EOPs total. If it is necessary to exceed the preferred maximum level of four (4) cases per PA, an equitable distribution of EOP cases within the unit will occur.
  8. Requesting Approval/Denial of Overtime and Workload Adjustment Modifications

    Ongoing communication between the US/designee and staff regarding workload is encouraged and expected to be bilateral.
    1. Requesting Overtime

      If, at any time during the month, staff believe that workload circumstances warrant overtime, they shall submit the request for overtime to the US or designee. Requests for overtime shall be made and approved, as noted below, in advance via the California Human Resource form titled “Authorization of Extra Hours” STD, Form 682 (Rev. 10/2019) available on the Intranet on the following page:

      http://intranet/ops/AO/dapo/DForms/Pages/std_forms.aspx

      In the event overtime is incurred as the result of unforeseen exigent circumstances, for example, a delay in booking an arrested parolee, participation in an unplanned arrest, unplanned/unavoidable after hour phone calls/contacts or other necessary but unanticipated after-hours work, the PA shall notify the US by telephone, as soon as it is reasonable and practical to do so. The PA shall submit a STD, Form 682 the next working day. The PA shall not be required to adjust their work schedule to avoid overtime.
    2. Approval of Overtime
      1. Paid overtime must be approved by the US or designee in advance except for exigent circumstances and unplanned/unavoidable/necessary after-hours work noted above. The US or designee shall document the date and time of the approved overtime on the STD Form 682, and shall provide a copy to the PA. The US or designee shall notate all approved overtime on the attached CDCR Form 2262 (11/12), District Overtime Report. Upon working overtime during the approved period, the PA is required to return the STD Form 682 to the US or designee, noting the actual hours worked (which shall not exceed the hours approved) and a brief synopsis of the duties completed, which would include the name, CDCR number and brief description of tasks.
      2. Tasks that can be approved for overtime include, but are not limited to:
        1. Coverage/workload of another PA’s caseload when that PA is out on leave or otherwise unavailable;
        2. Completing required reports such as violation, discharge or service referrals;
        3. Home contacts;
        4. Completing assigned pre-parole packets, including Pre-Release residence verification;
        5. Transportation and booking of a parolee, or picking up an incarcerated person from prison;
        6. Supervision of cases utilizing Electronic In-Home Detention;
        7. Completing TIRs, Interstate requests and in-custody interviews;
        8. Excessive OD coverage;
        9. Extensive parole supervision dedicated to one individual (i.e., EOP, CCC, DD3);
        10. Any other workload that is not directly attributable to an Agent’s assigned caseload.
    3. Denial of Overtime

      The reason for the denial of requested overtime will be documented in writing and provided to the PA.
    4. Workload Adjustment

      Modifications and Adjustments

      The US or designee shall review the workload summary to ensure that the weekly adjustments to workload are maintained appropriately and are equitable. However, at any time the PA has perceived that they are unable to meet the workload requirements, the PA shall case conference with the US or designee to address workload issues. There should be on-going face-to-face communication between case-carrying PA staff and the US or designee regarding workload modifications and adjustments.

      Workload adjustments may include correcting the status of an offender after a court action or transferring cases between PAs. If these workload adjustments still result in excess workload, additional adjustments, such as modifying case supervision specifications as identified below or authorization of overtime may be required. When case supervision specifications are modified, the US shall note which cases’ specifications have been modified for the month. When a US makes an adjustment to a caseload to comply with this provision, they must document the remedy taken for each caseload that was adjusted.

      The Department retains the discretion to determine which of the below options can be selected to adjust PA workload to manage CPSRM caseloads. When it is determined by the US that a workload/overtime adjustment is necessary, the US or designee shall:

      a. Modify case supervision workload specifications;
      b. Authorize paid overtime; or
      c. Utilize a combination of the above.
      If issues are not resolved after raising concerns at the local/Unit level regarding a failure to modify case supervision workload specifications and/or authorize paid overtime, CCPOA may elevate those concerns through the Regional chain of command, up to and including the ADD for further discussion.
    5. US or Designee (On the First Working Day of Month)
      1. Reviews all active and non-active cases on the roster.
        1. Meets with Parole Agents to reconcile caseload rosters to ensure parolees are appropriately classified.
        2. Reviews workload assigned to each PA on the Unit Workload Summary Report, to include the PA II.
        3. Caseload reconciliation should be an on-going process and is not restricted to the first working day of the month. However, the initial roster reconciliation at the first of the month must be completed.
      2. Waiver of Specifications

        The waiving of case contact specifications or other workload is the sole responsibility of the US. Each case must be considered on a case-by-case basis relative to the individual parolee’s case factors and specific needs. When tasks are waived, the US shall note this decision. The US shall normally refrain from waiving cases which present a de minimus impact on workload (i.e., in-custody cases) as defined by DAPO. The US may waive the following tasks:
        1. Home visits;

          (a) Home visits shall not be waived for the same parolee during two (2) consecutive months unless the parolee is homeless or the parolee resides in a geographically remote area (under these circumstances, the US, considering public safety, may waive this contact).

          (b) The US may waive the requirement of home visits being unannounced to allow the PA to notify the parolee in advance of the home visit. When this requirement is waived, the PA shall document the parolee’s notification on the Record of Supervision.
        2. Additional face-to-face contacts;
        3. Anti-narcotic tests;
        4. Significant collateral contacts;
        5. Resource contacts; and
        6. Pre-release residence verification – residence verification (CDCR Form 1658) must then be completed during the initial home visit.
      3. Except as provided below, the US may not waive the following tasks:

        (1) Initial interview;
        (2) Initial home visit (The US may, however, waive the time frame so that the Agent has more time to complete this task.);
        (3) Comprehensive interview;
        (4) Residence verification (CDCR Form 1658);
        (5) Goal and progress reports;
        (6) Case Conference Review (CDCR Form 1657) – Other than Case Conference Review while a parolee is in the transition phase, a parolee’s participation is not required during Case Conference Reviews;
        (7) Violation reports; or
        (8) Discharge review reports.
        The ADD, however, has the authority to waive any of the foregoing specifications, except violations reports and discharge review reports.
  9. Training Related Overtime

    Training shall be considered in determining whether overtime approval is necessary to allow PAs to meet specifications for their caseloads. However, overtime does not necessarily result from training. A PA III or PA II Supervisor determined to be a certified instructor in block training courses may be utilized in an effort to mitigate the need for overtime expenditures (e.g., Training for Trainers (T4T), Range Master/range safety, etc.).
  10. State Business

    PAs shall not conduct State business outside of approved scheduled work hours or approved overtime, as articulated in this provision.
  11. Remedies

    This section is subject to the grievance procedure delineated in Article VI of this Agreement, including full arbitration. However, remedies for a violation of this section shall not include monetary compensation, provided that the foregoing limitation shall not prevent issuance of a monetary remedy based on a finding of a simultaneous violation of one or more other sections of this Agreement.

19.09 PA Uniforms - Exposed Carry, Visible Identifiers, Uniforms and BPAA Attire

PAs will exercise discretion whether to be visibly armed in the community (exposed carry). In exercising this discretion, and in the interest of public safety, PAs will visibly display DAPO-approved identifiers and clearly identify themselves as Peace Officers in the community as the need arises. These identifiers will abide by the current best practices documented in current DAPO policy.

Parole Agent students assigned to the Basic Parole Agent Academy (BPAA) will be required to wear BPAA-approved and provided attire consisting of pants, a belt, and a polo shirt. If the student chooses to purchase their own academy attire, the attire must be approved by the BPAA Director, Commander or Coordinators consistent with DAPO policy. Students will also be required to provide their own athletic or boot style shoes.

19.10 DAPO Joint Labor-Management (JLM) Meetings and Meetings with the Director of DAPO/Undersecretary of Operations

  1. DAPO JLM: Unless mutually agreed otherwise by both parties, CCPOA (with up to four [4] members and a CCPOA Field Representative) and DAPO (with regional/statewide representatives and OLR in attendance) will conduct quarterly JLM meetings (with a hybrid virtual and in-person option) to discuss ongoing labor relations issues and maintain communication and dialogue regarding: contract administration and items of mutual interest or of concern to each party in an effort to resolve issues at the lowest level. Agendas may be requested by either party and will be provided no later than seven (7) business days prior to the JLM meeting. The parties reserve the right on a case-by-case basis to add time-sensitive, urgent items to the agenda. The party adding such last-minute items, however, shall come to the meetings with specifics and/or documents relating to the underlying issue. CCPOA members will be released on Official Business (OB) time and shall suffer no loss of compensation in connection with attending these quarterly meetings. Any mutually agreed upon additional attendees shall either be on their own time or RTB. The parties, upon mutual approval of the CDCR and CCPOA’s Chiefs of Labor, may schedule up to two (2) additional JLM meetings annually.

    PSA issues will be included in JLM meetings.
  2. Director Meetings: For the term of this agreement, the parties agree to continue an additional, higher-level meeting. CCPOA (with up to four [4] members and the CCPOA Chief of Labor or designee) may, in addition to the quarterly JLM above, request a quarterly meeting to be scheduled on a mutually agreed upon date with the DAPO Director and OLR to discuss issues, concerns or ideas regarding the following items:

    1. Safety Equipment (i.e., ballistic vest options that are concealable and appropriate for daily wear for PAs, Electronic Control Devices [ECDs], and protective equipment/kits);
    2. Communication Devices (i.e., exploring efficiency, efficacy, updates, upgrades, capabilities, maintenance and distribution of smart phones and radios and the potential use of tablets);
    3. Course of Fire requirements, training/remediation opportunities, scheduling range time and improving scheduling/communication protocols;
    4. PA Vehicles (i.e., storage capacity of vehicles, Vehicle Home Storage Permits, rules regarding PAs storing their vehicles overnight at a safe, preapproved location en route to their residence, code 3 lights within the CCU unit vehicle pool, vehicle replacement survey policy), and Department of General Services requirements/exceptions related to PA vehicles;
    5. Parole Agent Academy curriculum and length extensions;
    6. OB/RTB caseload reduction considerations;
    7. PSA issues not resolved at JLM above; and
    8. Exploration of Unit Preference Options for PAs.
    CCPOA will provide an agenda to the CDCR Chief of Labor no later than seven (7) business days prior to the Director meeting. The parties reserve the right on a case-by-case basis to add time-sensitive, urgent items to the agenda. The party adding such last-minute items, however, shall come to the meetings with specifics and/or documents relating to the underlying issue. CCPOA members will be released on Official Business (OB) time and shall suffer no loss of compensation in connection with these Director’s meetings. Any mutually agreed upon additional attendees shall either be on their own time or RTB.

    CCPOA may request that the Undersecretary of Operations attend a Director’s Meeting.

19.11 PA Vacation Scheduling and Use of Leave Credits

  1. During the period of October 1 through October 31 of each year, Agents may submit a vacation request for the following year to their supervisor. In the event that an Agent will be absent during the period listed above, they may submit their request to the supervisor prior to the leave. No later than December 1, the reviewing supervisor will approve or deny the vacation request in writing for the following calendar year. Requests to modify or rescind a previous vacation request must be submitted in writing no less than thirty (30) calendar days prior to the scheduled vacation.
  2. When multiple Parole Agents request the same vacation slots and the supervisor cannot grant the requests to all employees in the same Parole Unit making requests for the same vacation time, approval shall be granted in seniority order. For example, if four (4) Parole Agents submit vacation requests for the same time period and the supervisor determines that work conditions for the Parole Unit require that only three (3) Parole Agents can be absent during the time period, the three (3) most senior Parole Agents’ vacation requests will be approved.
  3. Single day leave usage requests shall be submitted with a PA’s monthly schedule and, if granted, will be based on BU 6 seniority. Any subsequent single day leave usage requests shall not be unreasonably denied and, if granted, will be on a first come first served basis.

19.12 CPSRM Parole Agent I Workload Study

DAPO contracted with University of California of Los Angeles (UCLA) to conduct a workload study for DAPO Parole Agent Is with CPSRM caseloads. A copy of the Final Report (not including all drafts or back-up documentation), which will include Workload recommendations, will be provided to CCPOA with forty-five (45) days of DAPO receiving it from the UCLA.

19.13 PSA Training

  1. PSAs will normally attend annual block training at their assigned institution or within the region of their assigned work location (which may be in-person or virtual at management discretion). Subject to availability, PSAs have the option of completing mandatory IST at local institutions, with approval from their immediate supervisor and the institutional IST coordinator. If staff use this option, they must obtain a copy of the signed CDCR 844 from the institutional IST coordinator for the completed training(s) and forward it to their designated training coordinator.
  2. The State will continue to provide online access to PSA-specific voluntary cross-training (e.g., COMPAS, ARMS, SOMS, ERMS, LMS, etc.), which will be conducted on the PSA’s own time.

19.14 CDCR PSA Workweek, Work Schedule, Travel Time

  1. The normal work schedule for CDCR PSAs shall be a four- (4-) day workweek (DAPO institutional and DRP PSAs) or five- (5-) day workweek (DAPO, BPH and DRP PSAs), as dictated by the workload, and approved by the supervisor in accordance with Subsection B. below. The PSA may schedule, with supervisor approval, other than an eight- (8-) or ten- (10-) hour day. The workweek shall start on Monday and end on Friday.

    PSAs may elect the daily start and stop times consistent with the supervisory approval contained in this Section.

    Except as emergency and operational needs dictate, work hours, subject to supervisor approval, will normally be scheduled between 0600 and 1800 (DAPO institutional PSAs); between 0700 and 1700 (BPH PSAs), and between 0800 and 1700 (DAPO Unit PSAs and DRP PSAs). The basis for denials due to emergency/operational needs shall be articulated in writing by the supervisor.
  2. Each PSA shall submit a proposed work schedule to the supervisor for each month at least seven (7) calendar days, but no more than fourteen (14) calendar days, prior to the beginning of the scheduled month for supervisors’ approval. The supervisor shall approve the work schedule at least three (3) days prior to the scheduled month, unless it can be documented that the scheduled work hours as submitted would be detrimental to the needs of the office or would hinder the PSA in the performance of their duties and responsibilities. This documentation shall be provided if requested by the employee. If the PSA does not submit a monthly work schedule, the supervisor will assign the work schedule.

    During the scheduled month, the supervisor may occasionally adjust the work hours based on operational needs with written justification to the PSA. This adjustment shall not be intended to avoid the assignment of voluntary overtime. PSA requested changes in the work schedules, excluding emergencies, will require prior supervisor approval. PSAs will advise the supervisor of emergency changes no later than the next workday.
  3. Travel Time

    The Community Transition Program (CTP) PSAs shall be paid beginning at the time of arrival at their assigned institution.
  4. The Department shall attempt to provide reasonable advance notice of scheduled mandatory training.
  5. PSAs directed to work beyond their scheduled and approved work hours will be paid appropriately and not have a subsequent shift shortened by management to avoid overtime.
  6. PSAs shall request overtime based on excess workload on an STD 682 that includes the justification for supervisory consideration. Denials shall be provided in writing to the employee with a copy of the initial request.

19.15 PSA Vacation Scheduling and Use of Leave Credits

  1. During the period of October 1 through October 31 of each year, PSAs may submit a vacation request for the following year to their supervisor. In the event that a PSA will be absent during the period listed above, they may submit their request to the supervisor prior to the leave. No later than December 1, the reviewing supervisor will approve or deny the vacation request in writing for the following calendar year. Requests to modify or rescind a previous vacation request must be submitted in writing no less than thirty (30) calendar days prior to the scheduled vacation.
  2. When multiple PSAs request the same vacation slots and the supervisor cannot grant the requests to all employees in the same worksite making requests for the same vacation time, approval shall be granted in seniority order. For example, if three (3) PSAs submit vacation requests for the same time period and the supervisor determines that work conditions for the worksite require that only two (2) PSAs can be absent during the time period, the two (2) most senior PSA’s vacation requests will be approved.
  3. Single day leave usage requests shall be submitted with a PSA’s monthly schedule and, if granted, will be based on BU 6 seniority. Any subsequent single day leave usage requests shall not be unreasonably denied and, if granted, will be on a first come first served basis.

ARTICLE XX CORRECTIONAL COUNSELORS

20.01 Correctional Counselor I Work Hours

  1. Work Schedules
    1. The normal work schedule for Correctional Counselor Is (CC Is) shall be either a four- (4-) day or five- (5-) day workweek, Monday through Friday up to a maximum of twelve (12) hours per day.
    2. CC Is may deviate/flex from the normal workdays or core hours (e.g., 0500-1300 or 1200-2000) with prior supervisory approval.
    3. Certain core hours that must be covered appropriately, may be set by individual institutions so long as the core hours fall between 0600 to 1800 and will be communicated to CC Is via memoranda.
  2. Each Correctional Counselor (CC I) shall submit a work schedule to the supervisor for each calendar month at least seven (7) calendar days, but no more than fourteen (14) calendar days, prior to the beginning of each work period. Schedules must reflect a total of forty (40) hours for the seven- (7-) day 7k work period. In submitting their schedule for supervisory approval, each CC I will propose whether or not they will take a lunch break during the period of time which is covered by that schedule. The supervisor shall approve the work schedule at the facility/complex using BU 6 seniority at least three (3) days prior to the scheduled work period, provided it meets the CC I’s duties, responsibilities and institutional need, and is consistent with Subsection A. above. If a requested work schedule is denied, the specific reasons for the denial will be given to the employee in writing or electronic communication. All denials must be based on case circumstances specific to a counselor’s duties rather than “blanket denials.” Denials of a work schedule shall not be based solely upon overdue casework. If the CC I does not submit a work schedule, the supervisor will assign the work schedule.

    A work schedule may be denied to fulfill the need to cover the core hours identified in Subsection A. above. The rejection of one or more schedules because of this need to cover core hours shall not be deemed a blanket denial.

    If there are no volunteers, the necessary core hour coverage shall be determined by inverse seniority.
  3. Current daytime schedules will be maintained unless deviation therefrom is mutually agreed to by the supervisor and employee. The institution may require CC I s, excluding camp counselors, working a given unit (on a non-overtime basis) to work up to one (1) evening per week (up to 2030 hours) based on legitimate institutional program needs. Evening work is defined as those hours worked after 1800 hours. None of this precludes scheduled or unscheduled overtime work.
  4. Positions that are required to attend the Interdisciplinary Treatment Team (IDTT) for Inpatient Psychiatric Care (e.g., mental health crisis bed and Psychiatric Inpatient Programs [PIP] with a fifty [50] or more bed capacity), which will be noted on the duty statements and job bulletins, may include one day of weekend work.

    Designated positions will not exceed two (2) and will either have Friday/Saturday or Sunday/Monday as RDOs.
  5. The supervisor may occasionally require a work schedule change for events that were not originally foreseen when the work schedule was originally submitted. This might occasionally include evening work or a weekend day, but shall be based on legitimate institutional program needs. The supervisor shall give a seven (7) calendar day prior notice for this temporary change. The notice shall be in writing and document the specific reasons for the change.
  6. Employee-requested changes in the work schedule will require supervisory approval.

20.02 Correctional Counselor I Workload

  1. CDCR shall provide equitable workload assignments for all CC Is within an institution. The status of CC I workload assignments shall be monitored by management, and appropriate steps will be taken to balance the workload. CC Is can request an accommodation via the Classification Services Unit (CSU) SharePoint site/comparable system that details with specificity the CC I’s concerns regarding timely completion of workload. The Hiring Authority/Correctional Counselor II (Supervisor) has a total of four (4) business days to respond via the CSU SharePoint site/comparable system and to adjust the CC I’s workload.

    The Hiring Authority or designee shall authorize overtime, when necessary, or a reasonable accommodation will be made to avoid unrealistic work expectations. The response shall be given to the requesting CC I within four (4) business days via the CSU SharePoint/comparable system. The overtime/reasonable accommodation may occur as a result of any of the following examples: the number and complexity of cases (including whether caseload is above the established ratios), institutional conversions/transfers, implementation of special programs/administrative bulletins, leaves of absence (including vacation), prolonged illness, out-of-class assignments, training of new employees and introduction of new technology or operational systems.

    CC Is utilized for short-term, non-emergency (e.g., cell searches, yard sweeps, or escorts) and acting assignments which preclude them from performing their full range of normal duties shall be reasonably accommodated by reassigning the duties to another CC I, postponing deadlines or authorizing overtime when a need exists. Short-term shall be defined as less than two (2) hours, not an entire shift, multiple days, or multiple CC Is to make up a day (e.g., each CC I does a two- (2-) hour shift until eight [8] hours is complete).

    A CC I shall not be expected to act as the supervisor in the Unit Classification Committee (UCC) when the supervisor is also on duty, except in extremely rare circumstances.
  2. The Hiring Authority shall fill vacant positions and/or new positions in a timely manner.
  3. In order to increase incarcerated person access to counselors, CCs shall be able to ducat incarcerated persons for classification and other related casework subject to administrative approval.
  4. The parties agree to convene an annual committee, to meet at the start of the calendar year, to review and assess possible redistribution of CC I workload.
  5. A copy of the semi-annual Correctional Counselor I Ratio Position Distribution Reports - Formal and Informal will be provided to CCPOA.
  6. The State agrees that separate and apart from the monthly Labor Management Meeting, local administrations will meet upon request with CCPOA Chapter President or designee and a CC I representative to discuss CC I workload issues. The parties agree that these meetings will occur no more than twice a month.

    If workload issues are not resolved at the local level, the Union can reduce their concerns to writing and meet/teleconference with the Assistant Deputy Director, Facility Support within ten (10) calendar days of the request. CCPOA’s documentation should be submitted to the CDCR Chief of Labor at least forty-eight (48) hours before the meeting.
  7. The State shall offer testing for the CC I classification every three (3) years pursuant to Government Code. The CC Is hiring list shall remain in effect until the next test is offered, unless otherwise proscribed in the Government Code.
  8. The parties agree that the SOMS agreement dated February 26, 2015, and subsequent SOMS agreements are hereby incorporated into this MOU by reference and are subject to MOU Section 27.01, Subsection C. for the term of this MOU.

20.03 Post and Bid by Seniority for Correctional Counselor Is

There shall be seventy percent (70%) of each institution’s budgeted CC I positions assigned by Unit 6 seniority (bid positions) and thirty percent (30%) shall be assigned by management (management positions). All bid/management CC I duty statements shall have a current description of the assigned position and location.
  1. CC I Eligibility for Post and Bid
    1. Must be a permanent full-time or Limited Term CC I.

      Limited Term CC Is are eligible to participate if CC I apprenticeship requirements have been completed.
    2. Performance evaluations will not be considered in determining eligibility or participation in the Post and Bid process.
    3. CC Is who laterally transfer and report on or before the bid process begins (i.e., first Monday in November) will be permitted to bid.
  2. Post and Bid Process

    Post and bid selections shall typically be in place for three (3) calendar years. For purposes of this MOU, the next bid is scheduled to commence in November 2025.
    1. Determining the 70/30 Split: A Local Joint Labor/Management Post and Bid Committee at each institution will meet to identify the total number of institutional posts, to include assigned position and location, which will be seventy percent (70%) of the total authorized posts listed on the Master Assignment Roster. The remaining thirty percent (30%) shall be designated as management positions. The following posts may be exempted from the Post and Bid process but will be included in the count for purposes of establishing the foregoing 70/30 calculations: (1) Restricted Housing Unit (RHU) posts at the CC I level and (2) Non-Case Carrying posts at the CC I level. Such determinations must be made no later than the first Monday of November.
    2. Seniority: On the first Monday in November, the Personnel Assignments Office (PAO) at each institution will post an updated seniority roster. CC Is alleging errors in the computation of seniority dates may file a complaint to the Personnel Assignments Lieutenant. If unresolved, the CC I may submit to the Hiring Authority for second (2nd) level review with resolution required within fourteen (14) days of the posting of the seniority roster. The second (2nd) level shall be the final level of review in the complaint process. Errors in favor of the CC I will result in the adjustment of the CC I seniority date at their institution.
    3. Posting of Positions/Bid Forms: On the second Monday in November, the PAO at each institution will make the standardized bid forms available and publish a listing of CC I positions available for bid that will include the date the bid forms are due. This list shall be posted publicly (e.g., outside the PAO, on a public bulletin board and/or the institutional share drive).
    4. Submission of Bid Forms: Completed CC I bid forms must be submitted to the PAO or designated PAO drop box or electronically to the PAO’s state email, on or before the close of business on the second Monday of December. At the time the CC I submits the bid form, it will be date-stamped and a copy given to the CC I. If submitted electronically, the date/time stamp in the email shall serve as proof of submission. The original will be retained in the PAO.
    5. Walk-Up Bid: Institutions may use a walk-up bid process. Any disputes regarding this process must be resolved at the local level.
  3. Time Frames
    1. Beginning the first Monday of December, the PAO shall have up to twenty-one (21) calendar days to determine the CC Is’ placement into the bid positions of their selection.
    2. No later than the first Monday of January, the PAO shall publish the listing of CC Is who were successful in their bid.
    3. At the time of publishing, a thirty- (30-) day window will be allowed for correcting errors. CC Is who believe they were placed into a position in error will have fourteen (14) calendar days to dispute the placement. Management will respond within ten (10) calendar days in writing and will make any necessary and appropriate adjustments.
    4. The PAO shall publish movement sheet(s) reflecting assignment changes. The assignment changes may occur as a single process or as locally agreed.
    5. Movement shall take place the first Monday of February in line with CC I caseload expectations.
  4. Caseload Expectations

    Prior to vacating their previously assigned position, CC Is shall work with their supervisor to ensure completion of casework (e.g., BITS, Annual Reviews, Initials/Intake).
  5. Continuous Bid Process

    If there is no interest in a vacant bid position, management shall fill the position by existing rules, policies and practices. For those positions retained by management, existing rules, policies and practices, with regard to filling vacancies, shall remain in effect.
    1. Vacant CC I positions will be posted on the first Monday of each month and remain posted for ten (10) calendar days. Any eligible CC I will be allowed to bid including those already in a bid position. No continuous bids will be accepted after the expiration of the ten- (10-) day posting period.
    2. Results for those who were successful in their continuous bid will be posted by the fourth Monday of each month. All job changes will have an effective date of not more than fourteen (14) calendar days from the date of the posting results.
    3. Subsequent to the initial Post and Bid, an otherwise eligible CC I may participate in the continuous bid process up to six (6) times during the bid period. Conditional bids count toward this limit. Bids due to deactivations shall not count towards this cap.
    4. CC Is who laterally transfer and have reported may continuous bid on any vacant bid position.
    5. After a CC I completes the apprenticeship program, they can participate in the continuous bid process.
  6. Conditional Bid Process

    The Conditional Bid Process will be the process in which CC I positions are filled on a temporary basis. Once it is determined that a CC I position could be temporarily vacant for more than thirty (30) calendar days, the CC I position will be posted for a “conditional bid”. A CC I displaced from a conditional bid may participate in the continuous bid process.
  7. Changes to Bid Position: A legitimate reason to change a bid position would be if the CC I bid position becomes a specialized unit requiring specific knowledge, skills and training for casework.
    1. The local Chapter President and/or designee and the affected CC I must be notified in writing prior to the change as to the specific reasons for the change. The CC I will have the first right of refusal for special training to do the special needs casework; therefore, no change would be necessary.
    2. The affected CC I may either: (a) remain in the position, (b) bid to a vacant bid position, or (c) request placement and be placed in any vacant management position. If the affected CC I accepts the management position, then the bid position reverts to management until the CC I returns to another bid position.
  8. Maintenance

    After the initial Post and Bid selections have been made, the following steps will be adhered to regarding maintenance of the process:
    1. If a bid position becomes vacant, the bid position will be filled through the continuous bid process.
    2. When a deactivation affects the number of positions on a Facility/Area, any CC I(s) displaced from a bid position(s) will be by inverse seniority. Disputes regarding this Subsection that cannot be resolved at the local level will be elevated through the CCPOA and CDCR Chiefs of Labor to the CCPOA Executive Vice President and CDCR Director for final resolution.
    3. Upon activation, all newly activated posts will be subject the 70/30 split. Newly designated bid positions will be subject to the continuous bid process.
    4. Upon written request of a CC I to vacate a bid position, management may, at its discretion, approve the CC I’s movement to a management position. Such movement will be without regard to schedules (watch, RDOs or start/stop times).
    5. A CC I shall be permitted to rebid to the same bid position. Should the CC I be successful in their bid attempt, the CC I will be subject to all provisions of this procedure as if assigned for the first time.
    6. Any bid position not bid during the bid period by an eligible CC I shall temporarily revert to management, and continue to be subject to the continuous bid process.
    7. When a CC I has been removed from their bid position as a result of adverse action related to job performance, the vacated position will be subject to the conditional bid process until the exhaustion of all applicable appeals. Upon the resolution of the adverse action process, unless the bid position is specifically removed as part of the adverse action, the CC I will be returned to their bid position.
  9. Disputes

    All disputes concerning Post and Bid issues that cannot be resolved at the local level shall be directed to the Joint Labor/Management Committee.
    1. All disputes concerning Post and Bid issues that are unable to be resolved at the local level shall be directed to the Joint Labor/Management Committee for final resolution, as the final level of review. The Joint Labor/Management Committee shall be comprised of equal representation of three (3) persons appointed by the Secretary or designee of CDCR and CCPOA, respectively. Disputes will be resolved by majority vote. In the event of a tie vote, the Secretary shall make the final determination.
    2. Any dispute regarding Post and Bid issues will begin with a grievance filed directly at second (2nd) level (Step 2). The affected CC I must file the grievance within twenty-one (21) days of the action giving rise to the dispute. The Hiring Authority must respond to the grievance within ten (10) days of filing. If the issue is not resolved at the local level, the grievance will be referred to the next available Joint Labor/Management Committee for resolution, unless the parties mutually agree otherwise.
    3. If the jurisdiction of the Joint Labor/Management Committee is in question, the grievance will be referred to the Joint Labor/Management Committee for resolution. Should the Joint Labor/Management Committee determine the issue is not related to Post and Bid, the grievance will be directed to the appropriate level for disposition. All decisions reached by the Joint Labor/Management Committee will be reduced to writing and implemented within fifteen (15) days unless otherwise mutually agreed to by the committee.
    4. The Joint Labor/Management Committee will meet as necessary to hold committee meetings. At least ten (10) days prior to the scheduled meeting, an agenda of the grievances to be heard and considered shall be provided to CDCR’s Chief of Labor. If there are two (2) or fewer grievances to be heard, the meeting will be cancelled and the grievances rescheduled. This meeting shall not be delayed for more than one (1) calendar month. The parties agree that the Joint Labor/Management Committee shall use their meeting time efficiently.
  10. RHU: A CC I who bids to an RHU cannot remain longer than two (2) years without an approved management exemption. When a CC I requests to stay longer, local management may, on an exception basis, approve an exemption.
  11. Management Rights: Nothing in this section shall diminish management’s right to carry out Departmental goals and objectives or interfere with management’s rights to meet operational needs. The afore-stated will not be done in an arbitrary or capricious manner.

20.04 Counselor Policy Committee

  1. The Counselor Policy Committee (CPC) shall continue during the term of this contract consistent with current practice, which may be modified upon mutual agreement. The CPC shall meet once every two (2) months unless mutually agreed by both parties to convene less or more frequently. No later than fourteen (14) days prior to CPC meeting, CCPOA shall provide a detailed agenda to CDCR OLR. Within seven (7) days from receipt of the agenda, Management will review and respond to the agenda provided and may also add agenda items as necessary.
    1. Any grievances resolved by CPC shall be considered a 3rd Level response and resolution. If the CPC resolves a grievance then the decision shall be final and binding on both parties.
    2. If the CPC 3rd Level resolution is not reasonably implemented within fifteen (15) calendar days, the issue shall be elevated to either the Associate Director (AD) or Deputy Director (DD) as follows:
      1. Local Issues: the appropriate AD for the affected facility shall respond within fifteen (15) calendar days.
      2. Statewide Issues: the DD of Operations of DAI Facility Operations. The AD/DD shall respond within thirty (30) calendar days. If unsatisfied with the AD/DD response, the grievance will be elevated to the next level consistent with Article VI.
    3. If the CPC is unable to come to a mutually agreed upon resolution/response to a grievance, the documented response indicating the reason shall be elevated to either the AD or DD as follows:
      1. Local Issues: the appropriate AD for the affected facility. If unsatisfied with the AD/DD response, the grievance will be elevated to the next level consistent with Article VI.
      2. Statewide Issues: the DD of Operations of DAI Facility Operations. The AD/DD shall respond within fifteen (15) calendar days. If unsatisfied with the AD/DD response, the grievance will be elevated to the next level consistent with Article VI.
  2. The State and CCPOA agree to maintain a committee consisting of up to three (3) Management employees and up to three (3) Rank & File employees for the purpose of the CPC. The parties by mutual agreement may include additional people as appropriate.
  3. All timelines in this section may be extended by mutual agreement of the parties.
  4. The CPC members shall receive a current copy of the Reasonable Workload Accommodation Report from the CSU SharePoint site on a monthly basis. Up to three (3) CPC members may receive eight (8) hours of time off, equally distributed between OB and RTB, to assess and research the issues presented in the Reasonable Workload Accommodation Report for up to the six (6) months per year that the CPC does not meet.
  5. The CCPOA CPC members shall receive remote access to SOMS for CPC related functions.
